For equilibrium, the additional force must balance this resultant: $F_x = -R_x$ and $F_y = -R_y$. Find its magnitude using $\sqrt{F_x^2 + F_y^2}$ and angle using $\tan^{-1}(|F_y/F_x|)$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the resultant horizontal component of the four forces:
$$R_x = 24 + 12\sin 30^\circ + 8\cos 30^\circ - 16\cos 30^\circ$$
$$R_x = 24 + 12(0.5) - 8\cos 30^\circ = 30 - 8\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 30 - 4\sqrt{3} \approx 23.0718\text{ N}$$

Calculate the resultant vertical component of the four forces:
$$R_y = 12\cos 30^\circ - 8\sin 30^\circ - 16\sin 30^\circ$$
$$R_y = 12\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) - 24(0.5) = 6\sqrt{3} - 12 \approx 10.3923 - 12 = -1.6077\text{ N}$$

For equilibrium, the additional force must have components:
$$F_x = -R_x \approx -23.0718\text{ N},\quad F_y = -R_y \approx +1.6077\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the additional force:
$$F = \sqrt{(-23.0718)^2 + (1.6077)^2} = \sqrt{532.308 + 2.585} = \sqrt{534.893} \approx 23.1\text{ N}$$

Calculate the direction angle above the negative x-axis:
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1.6077}{23.0718}\right) = \tan^{-1}(0.06968) \approx 3.99^\circ$$
teacher_walkthrough: To produce equilibrium, the single additional force $\mathbf{F}$ must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the resultant of the four given forces.
Step 1: Choose Cartesian axes with the positive $x$-axis pointing to the right and the positive $y$-axis pointing upwards.
Resolve each of the four forces:
1. Force of $24\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis: $X_1 = 24$, $Y_1 = 0$.
2. Force of $12\text{ N}$ at $30^\circ$ to the positive $y$-axis: $X_2 = 12\sin 30^\circ = 6\text{ N}$, $Y_2 = 12\cos 30^\circ = 6\sqrt{3} \approx 10.3923\text{ N}$.
3. Force of $8\text{ N}$ at $30^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis: $X_3 = 8\cos 30^\circ = 4\sqrt{3} \approx 6.9282\text{ N}$, $Y_3 = -8\sin 30^\circ = -4\text{ N}$.
4. Force of $16\text{ N}$ at $30^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis: $X_4 = -16\cos 30^\circ = -8\sqrt{3} \approx -13.8564\text{ N}$, $Y_4 = -16\sin 30^\circ = -8\text{ N}$.

Step 3: The balancing force $\mathbf{F}$ has components:
$$F_x = -R_x = -(30 - 4\sqrt{3}) \approx -23.0718\text{ N}$$
$$F_y = -R_y = -(6\sqrt{3} - 12) = 12 - 6\sqrt{3} \approx +1.6077\text{ N}$$

Step 5: Direction of $\mathbf{F}$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{|F_y|}{|F_x|} = \frac{1.6077}{23.0718} \approx 0.06968$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.06968) \approx 3.987^\circ \approx 3.99^\circ\text{ above the negative } x\text{-axis}$$
Thus, the additional force has magnitude $23.1\text{ N}$ and acts at $3.99^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis.
